title: Gartner warns much planned AI infrastructure spending may not earn its keep
friendlyTitle: Gartner says a lot of planned AI infrastructure may not pay for itself
summary: Gartner said more than $3.5 trillion of AI infrastructure spending could be exposed to impairment by the end of 2030 if current capital plans continue, because forecast AI revenue would not cover that spending and a 12% return. It also predicts that cost pressure will push more than 80% of independent neocloud providers to cease independent operations by 2030.
friendlySummary: Gartner predicts that more than $3.5 trillion of AI infrastructure spending could be at risk by 2030 if revenue does not catch up. It also expects most independent AI cloud specialists to stop operating on their own by then.
whyItMatters: Buyers of AI cloud capacity should not assume every new provider will still be independent in four years. The figures are a scenario, not a measured loss, but they are a reason to ask who owns the hardware and what happens to a workload if that provider is absorbed or shut.
friendlyWhyItMatters: If you buy AI computing from a new provider, ask who owns the machines and what happens if that company is sold or closes. This is a forecast, not a result that has already happened.
